purpose: Prove that committing the reviewed .gitattributes LF rules makes a fresh default Windows Git clone (core.autocrlf=true) check out docs/planning/showstake-v2/schema.sql with LF byte-for-byte equal to the recorded provenance hash; WITHOUT the committed attributes the same clone reproduces the exact CRLF drift the review observed.
method: 1. Confirm the effective Git setting: core.autocrlf=true (C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig, system-level) — the default Windows Git checkout behavior named in the review.

2. POSITIVE: create a temp repo (path WITH spaces) containing .gitattributes ('*.sql text eol=lf' plus .mjs/.json/.yaml/.md rules) and a copy of schema.sql, git add + commit, then `git clone` into a separate path WITH spaces.
3. Hash the clone's schema.sql raw bytes; count CRLF vs lone-LF.
4. NEGATIVE CONTROL: repeat the same clone WITHOUT .gitattributes to prove the counterfactual drift.
Commands were run with the stale GIT_CONFIG_* variables cleared; no home path was hardcoded; only temp paths under .local/ (whose parent repo path already contains spaces).
conclusion: The committed .gitattributes *.sql text eol=lf is the fix: it forces LF checkout under core.autocrlf=true, so verify-baseline.mjs's recorded provenance SHA (0e6afec5...) holds in a fresh clone. The negative control reproduces the reviewer's exact fresh_clone_crlf_sha (0571dd09...), confirming the diagnosis. A candidate overlay created AFTER checkout cannot retroactively re-line-ending existing files, so the attributes must be part of the committed tree BEFORE any fresh clone; this worker does not commit/push.
limits: Local Git/checkout proof only; no main commit/push performed by the worker. No historical hash or baseline/handoff byte was changed.
